value.rationale: The exact universal 14-vector threshold is an intrinsically motivated finite invariant of a recently posed composite-order Fourier phase-retrieval problem. It closes the first twice-prime case after the known ten-cycle threshold, lowers window length from six to five against the published general sufficient bound, supplies a matching obstruction, and treats arbitrary signals rather than sector-specific ones. The exhaustive cross-support incidence certificate is not a restatement of the known full-spark table; it directly resolves the missing quantifier for phase-retrieval design.
